title: Dynamic sounds capture PPS boundaries
citation: Canzoneri, E., Magosso, E., & Serino, A. (2012). Dynamic sounds capture the boundaries of peripersonal space representation in humans. PLoS ONE, 7(9), e44306.
notes: Canonical dynamic audio-tactile PPS task with 80 sound-overlap targets, 32 sound-present T0/T6 targets delivered in silence, and 76 auditory-only catches. The software recreates the moving sound virtually. Exact author gains, room transfer, tactile calibration and voice-key timing are unverified.

reference_parameters.baseline_subtype: Sound-present trial, silent at touch before or after the dynamic sound.
reference_parameters.response_rule: vocal response to tactile target, ignore sound
reference_parameters.analysis_outlier_rule: trim RTs exceeding 2 SD from participant/condition mean
reference_parameters.analog_apparatus_recreation: Original near/far speakers and SoundForge motion are modeled as the reported 110 cm to 10 cm moving-sound trajectory in the binaural renderer when exact author gain files are not available.
reference_parameters.reported_trial_formula: 80 sound-overlap targets (2 directions × 5 delays × 8 repetitions), 32 direction-coupled silent-at-touch targets (2 directions × 2 delays × 8 repetitions), and 76 auditory-only catches. Two blocks of 94, with the per-family block allocation unreported.
remaining_caveats: exact original SoundForge exponential gain/envelope files

provenance.source: PLOS ONE Methods report T1-T5 as 300, 800, 1500, 2200, and 2700 ms from sound onset.
PLOS ONE Methods report 112 tactile-target trials and 76 auditory-only catch trials split across two blocks.
PLOS ONE Methods report 3000 ms pink noise with near/far two-speaker exponential intensity manipulation.
